document.title: Excerpt from Record of Conversation between Mikhail Gorbachev and George Shultz, April 22, 1988
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: A week after the Geneva signing, Gorbachev reaffirms a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan and warns that Iranian PM Mousavi and an envoy of Zia ul-Haq spoke of deposing the regime and creating a fundamentalist union of Islamic countries. Shultz denies Pakistan wants that. Gorbachev calls Afghanistan a test of US-Soviet cooperation.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CPSU / Soviet leader

mentions.quote: GORBACHEV: Now, about Afghanistan. It seems to me that now the positions have become clearer.
SCHULTZ: I do not think Pakistan wants that.
Prime Minister Mousavi recently had received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq.
Zia and the United States are still tempted to try and overthrow the current regime in Kabul.

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: Head of the Afghan government in Kabul

mentions.quote: We, as much as we can, sympathize with Najibullah's efforts to form a coalition.

persons.name: Diego Cordovez
persons.role: UN mediator for the Geneva talks on Afghanistan

mentions.quote: We support Cordovez's efforts in creating an interim government.
we will entrust the remaining questions to you and E.A. Shevardnadze.
Please give my regards to the President.

events.description: Gorbachev and Shultz meet in Moscow and discuss Afghanistan, the Geneva Accords and preparations for a summit.
Iranian PM Mousavi reportedly received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq, discussing deposing the Kabul regime and a union of Islamic countries on a fundamentalist basis.
Geneva Accords on Afghanistan, with the USSR and US as guarantors, described as following the INF Treaty signing.
Gorbachev and Shultz conversation in Moscow on Afghanistan and US-Soviet relations.
Iranian PM Mousavi received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq, discussing deposing the regime and an Islamic union.
Geneva Accords on Afghanistan referenced as a big event following the INF Treaty.
Signing of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty referenced.
Gorbachev's one-on-one conversation with the President in Washington.

relationships.detail: Zia's messenger reportedly met Mousavi to discuss deposing the Kabul regime.
relationships.quote: Prime Minister Mousavi recently had received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq.

relationships.detail: Discussed the Afghan settlement and guarantees.
relationships.quote: if you decline to cooperate with us in achieving the goal of making Afghanistan a neutral, non-aligned state

relationships.detail: USSR sympathizes with Najibullah's coalition efforts, though it gets information through other channels too.
relationships.quote: We, as much as we can, sympathize with Najibullah's efforts to form a coalition.

relationships.detail: Najibullah heads the regime in Kabul.
relationships.quote: we do not get all our information from Najibullah

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says the US provides military assistance to the 'alliance'. Direction: alliance is recipient, US is provider.
relationships.quote: Now, the "alliance" intends to move to Iran. And you provide them with military assistance.

relationships.detail: Shultz says the US supports Cordovez's efforts to create an interim government.
relationships.quote: We support Cordovez's efforts in creating an interim government.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze and Shultz to continue work on remaining questions and summit preparations.
relationships.quote: E.A.Shevardnadze and I will continue our efforts in preparing the meeting at the highest level.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev and Shultz held a conversation in Moscow on 22 April 1988, described by Gorbachev as a meeting of old friends.
relationships.quote: Our conversation today was a meeting of old friends.

relationships.detail: Mousavi received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq and discussed deposing the current regime and creating a union of Islamic countries.
relationships.quote: Prime Minister Mousavi recently had received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq.

relationships.detail: Mousavi is identified as Prime Minister of Iran.
relationships.quote: As far as Iran is concerned, Prime Minister Mousavi recently had received a messenger from Zia-ul-Haq.

relationships.detail: Zia is treated as the head of Pakistan's policy; Gorbachev links Zia and Pakistan.
relationships.quote: It appears to me that the United States and Pakistan lack realism. Zia and the United States are still tempted

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says Zia and the US are both tempted to overthrow the Kabul regime.
relationships.quote: Zia and the United States are still tempted to try and overthrow the current regime in Kabul.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev groups the US and Pakistan as lacking realism and pursuing regime change in Kabul.
relationships.quote: the United States and Pakistan lack realism.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev accuses the US of seeking to depose the Kabul government and install a different regime.
relationships.quote: You sympathize with the cause of deposing him, putting another regime into place

relationships.detail: Najibullah is the leader whose coalition efforts the Soviets sympathize with.
relationships.quote: We, as much as we can, sympathize with Najibullah’s efforts to form a coalition.

relationships.detail: The USSR sympathizes with Najibullah's coalition efforts but gets information from other channels too.
relationships.quote: we do not get all our information from Najibullah; we receive a lot of interesting information through other channels

relationships.detail: USSR and the current Afghan government both favor a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: The Soviet Union, Afghanistan - and I mean its current government - are in favor of Afghanistan being a neutral, non-aligned state.

relationships.detail: Soviet Union and US act as guarantors of the Geneva Accords settlement.
relationships.quote: we are just acting as guarantors of the settlement.

relationships.detail: Cordovez is a mediator working on an interim government for Afghanistan (UN affiliation inferred).
relationships.quote: We support Cordovez’s efforts in creating an interim government.

relationships.detail: Shultz says the US supports Cordovez's efforts to create an interim government.
relationships.quote: We support Cordovez’s efforts in creating an interim government.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev says the US provides military assistance to the alliance.
relationships.quote: Now, the “alliance” intends to move to Iran. And you provide them with military assistance.

relationships.detail: The alliance intends to move to Iran.
relationships.quote: Now, the “alliance” intends to move to Iran.

relationships.detail: Shultz and Shevardnadze will continue preparing the highest-level meeting and discuss a ministerial meeting.
relationships.quote: E.A.Shevardnadze and I will continue our efforts in preparing the meeting at the highest level.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev entrusts remaining Afghanistan questions to Shultz and Shevardnadze.
relationships.quote: we will entrust the remaining questions to you and E.A. Shevardnadze.

relationships.detail: Shultz conveys messages to and from the President.
relationships.quote: Please give my regards to the President. Tell him that I am very pleased with our conversation.

relationships.detail: Gorbachev and the President had a one-on-one conversation in Washington.
relationships.quote: the same thing I told him during our one-on-one conversation in Washington

relationships.detail: Gorbachev speaks as leader of the Soviet Union.
relationships.quote: The Soviet Union, Afghanistan ... are in favor of Afghanistan being a neutral, non-aligned state.

relationships.detail: The current regime is in Kabul.
relationships.quote: overthrow the current regime in Kabul

key_claims: Gorbachev says the USSR and the Kabul government favor a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan.
Gorbachev accuses Zia and the US of still being tempted to overthrow the Kabul regime.
Gorbachev reports that Mousavi told a Zia messenger of Iran's position favoring a fundamentalist union of Islamic countries.
Gorbachev says the USSR gets information on Afghanistan through channels other than Najibullah.
Gorbachev claims the US provides military assistance to the Afghan 'alliance', which plans to move to Iran.
Shultz says the US supports a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan, refugee return and Cordovez's interim-government efforts.
Both sides present Afghanistan as a test case for Soviet-American cooperation after the INF Treaty.
